intro.title: Build client analytics tracker queue
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a client-side analytics tracker queue, a system that collects and temporarily stores user interaction data (like clicks or page views) before sending it to a server. You will learn how to implement a queue data structure using JavaScript arrays to manage these events in order. The core programming concepts involved include array methods, event handling, and asynchronous operations. By the end, you will have a functional queue that can add events, process them, and handle errors, all within a single JavaScript file.
intro.usecase: In modern web applications, analytics tracking queues are essential for collecting user behavior data without blocking the main thread. You'll see this pattern in e-commerce sites like Amazon, where product views and cart additions are tracked while maintaining smooth page interactions. Social platforms like Facebook use similar queues to record post engagements and ad clicks without disrupting the user experience. This approach ensures reliable data collection while keeping applications responsive during high-traffic periods.
